Example 26. In the figure, $ABCD$ is a square whose length of each side is 22 metre and region $AED$ is a half circle. Determine the area of the whole region.

Solution: Let the length of each side of the square $ABCD$ be $a$.

$\therefore$ Area of square region = $a^2$
Again, $AED$ is a half circle.

$\therefore$ Radius of the half circle $r = \frac{22}{2}$ metre = 11 metre.

Therefore, area of the half circle = $\frac{1}{2}\pi r^2$

$\therefore$ Area of the whole region = Area of the square $ABCD$ + area of the half circle $AED$

$= (a^2 + \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2)$

$= (22^2 + \frac{1}{2} \times 3.1416 \times 11^2) = 674.07$ square metre (approx.)

The required area is 674.07 square metre (approx.)

Example 27. In the figure, $ABCD$ is a rectangle whose length is 12 metre the breadth is 10 metre. and $DAE$ is a circular segment. Determine the length of the arc $DE$ and the area of the whole region.

Solution: The radius of the circular segment, $r = AD = 12$ metre and the angle subtended at centre $\theta = 30^\circ$.

$\therefore$ length of the arc $DE = \frac{\pi r \theta}{180}$

$= \frac{3.1416 \times 12 \times 30}{180} = 6.28$ metre (approx.)

Area of the circular segment $ADE = \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2$.

$= \frac{30}{360} \times 3.1416 \times 12^2 = 37.7$ square metre (approx.)

The length of the rectangle $ABCD$ is 12 metre and breadth is 10 metre.

$\therefore$ Area of the rectangle = length $\times$ breadth = $12 \times 10 = 120$ square metre

$\therefore$ Area of the whole region = $(37.7 + 120)$ square metre = 157.7 square metre (approx.)

The required area is 157.7 square metre (approx.).
